conditions.name: Deferral rule beats random at isolating hard cases
conditions.reason: deferred pile is +0.5 sd MORE lopsided than random (91.98% good vs 91.91% good in the auto-decided pile) - the router defers EASIER cases
notes: y_true == 1 means GOOD (approve-worthy, did not default).
Accuracy is measured against the no-deferral baseline: every case forced to approve/reject at the engine's own approval_threshold (CoDoC pattern).
balance_distance = |good_share - 0.5|; lower means a harder, more boundary-adjacent pile.
Random-router null: 200 uniform samples of the same deferral volume.
Caveat: balance_distance is a folded statistic, so its z-score is only interpretable when the population good-share is away from 50%. Here it is ~92% good, so the folding is immaterial.

conditions.name: Observed defer/override rate within the AUC-implied natural-rate bound
conditions.reason: observed defer rate 22.49% is 1.4x the upper bound 16.00% implied by AUC 0.765 - the router is referring far more cases than the model actually gets wrong, so most referrals are cases the model already handles

assumptions: binormal equal-variance scores; delta = sqrt(2) * Phi^-1(AUC)
natural ambiguous-case rate == Bayes error rate at the observed prior
upper bound = 2 x Bayes error (allows 50% referral precision)
lower bound = Bayes error (referrals must at least cover the errors)

notes: Approximation of Tasche, 'Bounds for rating override rates' (arXiv:1203.2287); not his exact construction.
Assumptions are listed in metrics.bound.assumptions and in the docstring of auc_implied_natural_rate_bound().
empirical_error_rate_no_deferral is reported so the binormal assumption can be sanity-checked against the data.

conditions.name: Exploration arm has enough un-selected labels
conditions.reason: no exploration arm data collected yet
notes: What is needed: the deferred_review capture table live in production with exploration_flag set on a random 2-5% of would-be-auto-decided applications;
at least 1000 of those exploration rows carrying a non-censored realized_outcome;
spanning enough time for outcomes to season, and recorded against a single engine_version / threshold_artifact_hash so a fixed router's labels can be separated from a broken router's.

conditions.name: Retraining design models selection mechanism and reviewer bias
conditions.reason: no retraining design document exists - nothing models the selection mechanism or reviewer bias, and the spec forbids writing one that treats human decisions as ground truth

required_topics: reviewer bias and consistency model (Madras et al.)

notes: Not computable from prediction_outputs.csv: this is a design artifact, not a statistic. Reported FAIL rather than UNKNOWN because absence of the document is itself conclusive.

To satisfy it, a written design must cover: selection mechanism / missingness model (RMT-Net); reviewer bias and consistency model (Madras et al.); explicit rejection of human_decision-as-ground-truth.
Per spec section 3 this design should not be built until conditions 1-3 hold.
